text:
Jacek Karpiński was a Polish computer scientist and engineer known for pioneering work in the field of computers during the communist era. Born in 1927 in Turin, Italy, he was the son of an aeronautic engineer and a physician, both pioneers in winter mountaineering. His early life was marked by a severe injury during World War II, where he lost sight in both eyes and sustained partial hand amputation while working on homemade bombs for the Polish underground resistance. Despite these challenges, he recovered and became a significant figure in Polish computing history.
Karpiński's most notable achievements include the design of the AKAT-1, the world's first transistor-based differential equations analyzer in 1959, and the KAR-65, a high-speed asynchronous computer capable of 100,000 operations per second. He later founded the Microcomputers' Construction Plant to develop the K-202, a revolutionary minicomputer that utilized Intel 4004 chips and advanced memory segmentation. Although the K-202 was technically superior to contemporary Western machines and produced only 30 units due to political and economic constraints within Poland, it remains a landmark in the history of computer architecture. His life ended on February 21, 2010, in Wrocław, Poland.
